label: Mistral-7B
text:
```
find / -perm -4000 -type f
```

This command finds all SUID binaries (binaries with the set-user-ID bit set) in the entire file system. The `-perm` option checks file permissions, the `-4000` specifies the SUID permission, and the `-type f` option filters for files (not directories). The `/` at the beginning of the path is the root directory.

text:
```bash
sudo find /home -type f -perm -0002 -exec chmod 0640 {} \;
```

This command will find all world-writable files under the /home directory and change their permissions to readable-writable-owned (640). If you want to find and change the permissions of directories as well, replace `-type f` with `-type f -o -type d`. However, it's generally not recommended to make directories writable by others.
